newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine province mulls farm mortgage-backed bond.
newsitem.headline: Argentine province mulls farm mortgage-backed bond.

text.p: Argentina's province of Mendoza is hoping to launch a bond backed by its agricultural credit portfolio, the province's economy minister said Tuesday.
"We have to look for new financing," Economy Minister Ana Maria Mosso de Mortarotti told Reuters.

Since the prvatization of public banks by Mendoza in 1995, the province has issued debt to cover short-term financing and it is now considering issuing more to pay for the amortization and interest costs of the outstanding debt.
The idea is to "issue a bond guaranteed by agriculture," Mosso de Mortarotti said.

The province has a large portfolio of agricultural credits, and the new bonds would be backed by the mortgages on the farm land, explained Mosso de Mortarotti. The size of the issue may be between $120 million and $200 million, she said.
But she said that "to construct a guarantee (of this kind) is not easy," and that is why the province is now looking for underwriters to help structure the bond.
Mosso de Mortarotti expects the launch to be ready in four to five months.
Mendoza already led the way in the Argentine capital markets in August when it became the first province to issue bonds backed by oil royalties, from five oil concessions in the province.
The province sold $150 million worth of debentures due 2002. The lead manager was Lehman Brothers International.
